The main takeaway from our work is that

bryophyte stomatal evolution has not been studied from a functional perspective and the data we present here suggest that the stomatal apparatus of mosses and liverworts is fundamentally different from that of tracheophytes and that this difference is related to their water relations.
the stomatal apparatus is an ancient feature, which has been subject to multiple origins and multiple functional roles, the latter of which are not limited to the control of CO2 uptake.
